verdict: This portfolio maps the Bangalore initiative across customer experience, pricing, infrastructure, monitoring, strategy, analysis, assisted booking and production migration. Select any row to see its purpose and linked delivery evidence.

portfolio_summary.definition: Launch rate means all agreed acceptance criteria are live and verified: 2 of 7 projects. Five of seven already have usable production foundations.

initiative_projects.name: Orbit
initiative_projects.role: Turns search demand into understandable, priced and bookable Bangalore journeys.
initiative_projects.what: Orbit is the customer-facing product: market hubs, route pages, airport transfers, packages, search, quote selection and checkout handoff.
initiative_projects.why: The legacy and early V2 experiences used inconsistent URLs, search controls and journey state. Customers and Google needed one coherent Bangalore product surface.
initiative_projects.enables: Customers can discover a Bangalore product, understand the journey and fare, and continue to booking without losing route, airport or package context.

milestones.name: Public URL and Market Hub foundation
milestones.what: Established the V2 public URL contract, served market and route leaders, separated market hubs from local rental and rebuilt the journey composer.
milestones.why: The first Bangalore pages did not have a stable public identity or uniform journey entry point.
milestones.enables: A coherent market hub with durable URLs and one booking interaction model.

milestones.name: Route pricing, trust and discovery
milestones.what: Made fares, quote basis, dates, distances, vehicle pages, place cards, guides, reviews and priority routes clearer.
milestones.why: A route page that hides or changes its fare cannot reliably convert high-intent search traffic.
milestones.enables: Customers can compare a credible journey and proceed with fewer pricing surprises.

milestones.name: Bangalore SEO, sitemap and canonical migration
milestones.what: Created the eligible Bangalore sitemap, consolidated URL families, protected canonical/metadata contracts and concentrated internal discovery.
milestones.why: Duplicate and weak URLs divided search authority and allowed routine changes to damage ranking identity.
milestones.enables: Google receives one reviewed inventory of 44 indexable Bangalore URLs.

milestones.name: Website funnel and Concierge handoff
milestones.what: Instrumented route-level funnel events, persisted Bangalore attribution and embedded Concierge while keeping Bangalore navigation inside Orbit.
milestones.why: Landing sessions were disconnected from quote, checkout and booking outcomes.
milestones.enables: Privacy-safe acquisition-to-booking measurement once production collection and reconciliation are complete.

milestones.name: Tier 1 airport product and checkout
milestones.what: Launched the reviewed locality directions and separated airport, terminal, fare area, exact address, flight and dispatch concepts.
milestones.why: Airport journeys lost direction and operational context and could silently apply incorrect local pricing.
milestones.enables: A customer can price and book airport-locality or airport-outstation travel with useful dispatch details.

milestones.name: Bookable taxi package experience
milestones.what: Launched canonical package detail and exact vehicle/date/traveller quote controls.
milestones.why: Legacy package content was not a reliable, transparent or canonical booking product.
milestones.enables: A reusable path from package discovery to an exact server-priced quote.

milestones.name: Shared engineering invariants
milestones.what: Referenced the cross-repository safety and ownership rules inside Orbit.
milestones.why: Implementation rules must remain consistent across independently deployed services.
milestones.enables: Changes are reviewed against shared contracts rather than repository-local assumptions.

initiative_projects.name: Nexus
initiative_projects.role: Owns canonical identities, SEO content, quotes, package products and route economics decisions.
initiative_projects.what: Nexus is the server-side source of truth used by customer channels.
initiative_projects.why: Pages and channels cannot safely invent route identity, availability, content or commercial decisions independently.
initiative_projects.enables: Orbit and Concierge consume consistent products, prices and lifecycle identities.

milestones.name: SEO content platform
milestones.what: Built typed SEO read models, storage, safe publishing, imports, caching, correction and airport identities.
milestones.why: Search content needed one governed and versioned source.
milestones.enables: Consistent content across Orbit page families with auditable changes.

milestones.name: Canonical market and lifecycle contracts
milestones.what: Defined canonical route/market identity and carried it into quote and booking lifecycle events.
milestones.why: Cross-system measurement fails when the same journey has different identifiers.
milestones.enables: Reliable joins between acquisition, quote, booking and economics.

milestones.name: Transparent route pricing and availability
milestones.what: Exposed round-trip basis, removed zero-configured vehicles and classified quote availability/inbound gaps.
milestones.why: Opaque or impossible quotes damage trust and hide product gaps.
milestones.enables: Customer pages can explain fares and distinguish unavailable routes from system failures.

milestones.name: Route economics ledger and guardrails
milestones.what: Added deterministic contribution, freshness rules, guardrails and immutable persisted economics decisions.
milestones.why: Traffic or bookings do not prove that a route makes money.
milestones.enables: Runtime scale/pause decisions after actual supplier costs and outcomes are reconciled.

milestones.name: Taxi package domain, pricing and publication
milestones.what: Built package lifecycle, revisions, rate cards, immutable quotes, inventory import and published detail APIs.
milestones.why: Packages needed a real product model rather than ungoverned legacy content.
milestones.enables: Transparent, versioned and bookable Bangalore packages.

milestones.name: Reputation snapshots
milestones.what: Added manually imported, source-aware Google reputation snapshots.
milestones.why: Customer trust claims must be genuine and traceable rather than authored constants.
milestones.enables: Orbit can progressively render real review evidence.

milestones.name: Deployment and shared invariants
milestones.what: Protected Nexus behind Nginx, fixed rollback revision capture and adopted shared engineering rules.
milestones.why: Production changes need safe routing and recoverable deploys.
milestones.enables: Controlled releases and consistent system boundaries.

initiative_projects.name: Terra
initiative_projects.system: Infrastructure as code and production collection
initiative_projects.role: Owns safe, reviewable production infrastructure such as telemetry collection, ALB and WAF configuration.
initiative_projects.what: Terra converts manually managed AWS and observability configuration into declarative, reviewable desired state.
initiative_projects.why: Console-only infrastructure changes are difficult to audit, reproduce and roll back.
initiative_projects.enables: Safe plan/apply workflows with explicit production ownership.

milestones.name: Production Alloy ownership
milestones.what: Moved production telemetry collector configuration and rollout controls into Terra.
milestones.why: Application metrics need a managed collection path.
milestones.enables: Orbit and Nexus telemetry can be scraped consistently once host activation is completed.

milestones.name: ALB rules as code
milestones.what: Adopt existing ALB listener rules and create a protected deployment pipeline.
milestones.why: Manual sitemap and application routing rules can drift or conflict by priority.
milestones.enables: Reviewed, reproducible routing changes instead of ad-hoc console edits.

milestones.name: AWS WAF management
milestones.what: Add declarative WAF plans, protected apply, OIDC and remote state.
milestones.why: Security rules require change history and safe deployment boundaries.
milestones.enables: Auditable WAF changes with reduced credential and rollback risk.

milestones.name: Shared engineering invariants
milestones.what: Adopted common engineering and production rules.
milestones.why: Infrastructure must follow the same ownership and safety model as applications.
milestones.enables: Consistent review expectations across the stack.

initiative_projects.name: Beacon
initiative_projects.role: Turns service telemetry into route-level funnel, pricing, SEO and data-quality visibility.
initiative_projects.what: Beacon is the operating observability layer for cross-system questions and alerts.
initiative_projects.why: Events are not useful until production collection and reconciliation prove completeness.
initiative_projects.enables: Operators can detect broken funnels, stale prices, missing data and SEO regressions.

milestones.name: Secure deployment and operations
milestones.what: Deployed Beacon securely and documented how it is operated.
milestones.why: Monitoring must itself be durable and supportable.
milestones.enables: A stable internal service for operational queries.

milestones.name: Attributed Bangalore funnel query
milestones.what: Added a market/channel query for landing, quote, availability, checkout and booking stages.
milestones.why: Daily reports need one bounded view of Bangalore organic progression.
milestones.enables: Comparable funnel windows once all metric series are collected.

milestones.name: Funnel, pricing, SEO and data-quality monitoring
milestones.what: Build reconciled dashboards, synthetic journeys and actionable alerts.
milestones.why: Missing telemetry currently prevents commercial confidence.
milestones.enables: Trusted production health and rapid detection of revenue-impacting regressions.

milestones.name: Durable multi-user operations
milestones.what: Harden Beacon for sustained use by multiple operators.
milestones.why: An operating scorecard must not depend on one developer session.
milestones.enables: Repeatable team access and operational continuity.

initiative_projects.name: Compass
initiative_projects.role: Keeps the cross-repository work inside one market initiative and defines when to scale, maintain or pause.
initiative_projects.what: Compass is the management layer: objective, dependencies, owners, gates and review cadence.
initiative_projects.why: Many successful technical deliveries do not automatically create a successful market launch.
initiative_projects.enables: A single accountable plan across product, pricing, operations, acquisition and analytics.

milestones.name: Bangalore B2C Market Hub epic
milestones.what: Created the parent initiative and cross-linked its repository workstreams.
milestones.why: Orbit, Nexus, Terra, Beacon and supporting projects needed one shared outcome.
milestones.enables: One place to assess delivery and the remaining commercial loop.

milestones.name: 90-day route rollout
milestones.what: Define owners, launch gates and day-30/60/90 route decisions.
milestones.why: Expansion must be gated by margin, acquisition cost, supply and completion quality.
milestones.enables: Evidence-led scale, maintain or pause decisions.

milestones.name: Shared engineering invariants
milestones.what: Referenced shared cross-repository implementation rules.
milestones.why: The strategy layer must point to the same boundaries used by delivery teams.
milestones.enables: Consistent governance language across initiatives.

initiative_projects.name: Atlas
initiative_projects.role: Models canonical market architecture and combines acquisition, product and commercial evidence for decisions.
initiative_projects.what: Atlas is the analysis and operating-intelligence project supporting SEO, package launch and route decisions.
initiative_projects.why: Cross-system delivery needs an independent model of what is live, measurable and commercially ready.
initiative_projects.enables: Audits, launch gates and route-level scorecards across the portfolio.

milestones.name: Canonical Bangalore URL architecture
milestones.what: Modelled canonical and alias URL families across Bangalore products.
milestones.why: Sitemap, routing and measurement must refer to the same products.
milestones.enables: Auditable migration and page-family coverage.

milestones.name: Route operating scorecard
milestones.what: Combine route, segment and channel demand with completion and contribution.
milestones.why: GA4 and GSC alone cannot determine where the business should scale.
milestones.enables: A repeatable operating and decision cadence.

milestones.name: Nexus SEO read-model migration
milestones.what: Track adoption, imports, parity, telemetry and legacy fan-out removal.
milestones.why: The new content authority is only complete when every public family uses it safely.
milestones.enables: A single governed SEO platform with resilient serving.

milestones.name: Bangalore taxi packages launch
milestones.what: Coordinate domain, pricing, pages, content, operations, measurement, SEO and launch QA.
milestones.why: A package is not launch-ready from a page and price alone.
milestones.enables: A reviewed first wave of ten bookable Bangalore packages.

milestones.name: Bangalore SEO recovery and funnel diagnosis
milestones.what: Track crawl access, organic demand conversion and missing checkout/booking events.
milestones.why: Growing impressions are wasted if landing and funnel failures are invisible.
milestones.enables: Prioritised fixes based on production demand and lost conversion.

milestones.name: Shared engineering invariants
milestones.what: Documented the common system rules in Atlas.
milestones.why: Audits must evaluate every repository against consistent constraints.
milestones.enables: Comparable cross-system findings.

initiative_projects.name: Concierge
initiative_projects.role: Carries customer journey context into assisted sales and human handoff.
initiative_projects.what: Concierge is the assisted booking product used from the website and WhatsApp.
initiative_projects.why: Many cab customers need help, but assisted enquiries were disconnected from acquisition and booking outcomes.
initiative_projects.enables: A durable assisted journey with pricing parity and future end-to-end attribution.

milestones.name: Automated deployment
milestones.what: Added GitHub-driven production deployment with a self-hosted runner.
milestones.why: The assisted channel needed a reproducible release path.
milestones.enables: Controlled Concierge releases.

milestones.name: Website channel and journey context
milestones.what: Created the website channel, Orbit context contract and native drawer integration.
milestones.why: Customers should not repeat route information when requesting assistance.
milestones.enables: Context-aware handoff from Orbit into Concierge.

milestones.name: Durable sessions
milestones.what: Replaced temporary session behavior with Redis-backed storage.
milestones.why: Assisted conversations must survive process restarts and multi-step journeys.
milestones.enables: Reliable ongoing customer conversations.

milestones.name: Pricing parity
milestones.what: Fixed round-trip quote parity between Concierge and Nexus.
milestones.why: Assisted and website channels must not quote different prices.
milestones.enables: Consistent customer promises across channels.

milestones.name: WhatsApp launch and attribution
milestones.what: Complete production configuration, reliability, human handoff and enquiry-to-booking attribution.
milestones.why: A visible website drawer is not the same as a production-ready assisted sales channel.
milestones.enables: Measured WhatsApp acquisition through completed booking.

milestones.name: Shared engineering invariants
milestones.what: Adopted shared engineering rules.
milestones.why: Assisted booking must honor the same pricing, identity and safety boundaries.
milestones.enables: Consistent integration across channels.

initiative_projects.name: Legacy frontend, AWS and Google Search Console
initiative_projects.role: Removes duplicate legacy ownership, routes new city assets correctly and confirms Google discovery.
initiative_projects.what: This lane covers the Bitbucket frontend cleanup, manual ALB listener rules and Search Console submissions that connect the new stack to production and Google.
initiative_projects.why: A new sitemap inside Orbit has no effect if legacy still publishes the same URLs or the load balancer sends requests elsewhere.
initiative_projects.enables: One production source for each city sitemap and a measurable Google discovery window.

milestones.name: Legacy Bangalore sitemap cleanup
milestones.what: Removed superseded Bangalore source URLs from gmc_frontend.
milestones.why: Google should not receive competing inventories from old and new stacks.
milestones.enables: Orbit becomes the clean Bangalore sitemap owner.

milestones.name: ALB city sitemap routing
milestones.what: Added listener rules for /sitemap-bangalore.xml and /sitemap-vijayawada.xml to the new target group.
milestones.why: The public URLs had to reach the Orbit deployment.
milestones.enables: Stable public sitemap endpoints while Terra adoption is pending.

evidence.label: Bangalore rule priority 27 and Vijayawada rule priority 28

milestones.name: Google Search Console submission
milestones.what: Submitted both city sitemaps and confirmed successful discovery.
milestones.why: Publishing alone does not tell us whether Google fetched the inventories.
milestones.enables: Settled 14/28-day indexing and ranking measurement.

milestones.name: Production deployment and smoke verification
milestones.what: Deployed Nexus migrations and Orbit, then verified Tier 1 pages and the 44-URL sitemap.
milestones.why: Merged code is not evidence that the customer-facing product is live.
milestones.enables: Production acceptance evidence for the initiative.

executive.status_truth: The customer and search foundations are live. Profitability and completed-trip performance cannot yet be verified.
executive.decision_required: Assign owners and target dates to the commercial truth loop
executive.decision_reason: Actual-cost reconciliation, assisted attribution, production monitoring and scale gates span several systems. Without named accountability, product delivery can continue while the business decision remains blocked.

brief.label: What is live
brief.detail: Bangalore hub, routes, airport products, packages, 44-URL sitemap, canonical contracts and website funnel producers are in production.

brief.label: Early market signal
brief.detail: Seven-day Bangalore clicks rose from 24 to 49. This is promising discovery movement, not yet proof that the new work caused bookings.

brief.label: Main blocker
brief.detail: Confirmed bookings, completed trips, supplier actuals, refunds and contribution are not yet reconciled into one trusted view.

brief.label: What happens next
brief.detail: Finish instrumentation and economics, observe settled SEO and funnel data, then make route-level scale, maintain or pause decisions.

differences.before: Pages and sitemap ownership were split between legacy frontend and the new stack.
differences.now: Orbit owns a reviewed, eligibility-driven Bangalore inventory; legacy entries were removed and ALB routes one sitemap.
differences.why: Concentrate crawl and ranking authority instead of asking Google to reconcile duplicates.

differences.before: Pages could invent or silently change route identity, SEO fields and canonical URLs.
differences.now: Nexus owns canonical identities and content; Orbit protects search-critical contracts with executable tests.
differences.why: Make every route measurable and prevent routine UI changes from resetting SEO progress.

differences.before: Airport fare area, exact address, direction, terminal and flight details were conflated or lost.
differences.now: Each concept has a clear role and persists from search through quote, checkout and dispatch.
differences.why: Price against controlled geography while giving operations the exact trip information they need.

differences.before: Success was discussed through traffic, bookings or code shipped in isolation.
differences.now: Delivery, acquisition, funnel conversion, completed-trip economics and readiness gates are separate layers.
differences.why: Avoid scaling routes that attract traffic but fail operationally or lose money.

differences.before: Monitoring was an application concern with incomplete production ownership.
differences.now: Orbit emits bounded metrics, Terra owns collection and Beacon owns cross-system queries and alerts.
differences.why: Give every observability layer one accountable owner and make missing data visible rather than treating it as zero.
